open_points.subject: sandbox process limit
open_points.text: ResourceBounds M04 are enforced with `setrlimit` (... processes), set inside the environment before the code loads
open_points.question: What exactly does `process_count` count, and what RLIMIT_NPROC value must the sandbox set when its runner is itself a process?
options: `process_count` counts processes created by user code, so the runner sets the limit to `process_count + 1`
`process_count` includes the runner, so the limit is set to exactly `process_count`
`process_count` limits all processes attributed to the namespace user, including infrastructure processes
open_points.default_guess: Count user-code processes and set the limit to `process_count + 1` for the runner.

open_points.subject: scratch aggregate bound
open_points.text: each scratch file's size ...; how is the sandbox's own
open_points.question: Is only each individual scratch file bounded by `sandbox_scratch_bytes_max`, or must the exchange directory also have an aggregate byte bound?
options: Only a per-file bound; the directory has no aggregate bound
A per-execution aggregate bound equal to `sandbox_scratch_bytes_max`
open_points.default_guess: Enforce only the stated per-file bound and no aggregate directory bound.

open_points.subject: scratch-limit detection
open_points.text: a limit hit (memory, process count, scratch, `output_bytes`) — `resource_exhausted`
open_points.question: What constitutes a scratch limit hit when a write is refused or partial, the code catches the error, or the process receives or changes the disposition of the file-size signal?
options: Any kernel-attributed attempt to exceed the file-size limit makes the execution `resource_exhausted`, even if caught
Only termination by the file-size limit is `resource_exhausted`; a caught write error may still allow success
A caught write error is not a limit hit, while termination by the signal is `crashed`
open_points.default_guess: Record any kernel-attributed file-size-limit denial as `resource_exhausted`, regardless of whether code catches the error.

open_points.subject: host scratch exhaustion
open_points.question: If a scratch write fails because host storage is exhausted rather than because the per-file limit was reached, what outcome and isolation guarantee apply?
options: It is an ordinary code error and becomes `crashed` only if it escapes `run`; no host-storage isolation is promised
It is a scratch limit hit and therefore `resource_exhausted`
The sandbox must provision an isolated aggregate quota so host storage exhaustion cannot be exposed directly
open_points.default_guess: Treat host-storage exhaustion as an ordinary raised error and promise no isolation beyond the stated per-file bound.

open_points.subject: sandbox start probe
open_points.question: Which resource-bound values and limit-setting cases must `probe_sandbox` exercise before the kernel is allowed to start?
options: All current release ceilings, including every setrlimit-controlled resource
A fixed minimal probe chosen by the sandbox implementation
One representative contract-sized set of bounds
Only bubblewrap isolation and Python execution, without verifying every limit
open_points.default_guess: Probe using the current release ceilings and verify that every required limit can be set.
